_readme: Round 5 of 20 popular Gutenberg titles. Skipped: The Heart of Midlothian (Scott) - only available inside a 'World's Greatest Books' anthology, not standalone on Gutenberg. Hudson River Bracketed (Wharton) - not on Gutenberg at all. A Harlot High and Low (Balzac) - already in DB as 'Splendeurs et misères des courtisanes'.

books.title: Barry Lyndon
books.author: William Makepeace Thackeray
books.synopsis: An Irish adventurer schemes, duels, and gambles his way from obscure poverty into the English aristocracy by marrying the widowed Countess of Lyndon, narrating his own rise and ruin without a shred of self-awareness of his villainy.

books.title: Pendennis
books.author: William Makepeace Thackeray
books.synopsis: A vain, impressionable young man drifts from an actress's spell through Oxford disgrace, London literary hackwork, and society courtship, guided and repeatedly rescued by his devoted uncle and the patient Laura.

books.title: The Newcomes
books.author: William Makepeace Thackeray
books.synopsis: Colonel Thomas Newcome, an honest old India veteran, returns to London society and watches his artist son Clive's love for their cousin Ethel founder on family pride and money, as the Colonel's own fortune and health decline.

books.title: Omoo
books.author: Herman Melville
books.synopsis: A sailor and his companion Doctor Long Ghost, cast ashore after a mutiny in the South Seas, drift through Tahiti and its islands as beachcombers, jailed loosely by half-hearted French and native authorities and living by their wits.

books.title: Mardi
books.author: Herman Melville
books.synopsis: A sailor jumps ship with a harpooner companion and, after rescuing an island maiden, drifts into the archipelago-kingdom of Mardi, an allegorical voyage through invented islands each satirizing a nation, philosophy, or folly of the real world.

books.title: Redburn
books.author: Herman Melville
books.synopsis: A naive young gentleman's son signs on as a green hand aboard a merchant ship to Liverpool, enduring the brutal hazing of the forecastle and discovering the squalor of the docks his father once described in genteel guidebook terms.

books.title: White-Jacket
books.author: Herman Melville
books.synopsis: A sailor nicknamed for the makeshift white jacket he sews himself narrates a voyage home aboard a U.S. Navy frigate, cataloguing its floating world of flogging, rank, and shipboard justice.

books.title: The Confidence-Man
books.author: Herman Melville
books.synopsis: Aboard a Mississippi steamboat on April Fool's Day, a shape-shifting swindler works through a series of disguises to test the credulity and charity of his fellow passengers, in Melville's bleak, riddling satire on trust and belief.

books.title: Fanshawe
books.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
books.synopsis: A frail, bookish college student at a small New England school falls for a guardian's ward pursued also by a genial rival and a sinister stranger, and dies quietly after saving her from abduction. Hawthorne's anonymously published, later disowned first novel.

books.title: St. Ives
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.synopsis: A French prisoner of war escapes an Edinburgh castle during the Napoleonic Wars and flees across Britain in disguise, chasing an inheritance and a sweetheart while a relentless pursuer closes in.

books.title: The Ebb-Tide
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson and Lloyd Osbourne
books.synopsis: Three destitute beachcombers in Tahiti take charge of a schooner under false pretenses meaning to sell its cargo of champagne, and find the island they're sent to is ruled by a deranged, charismatic trader with his own designs on them.

books.title: Weir of Hermiston
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.synopsis: A stern Scottish hanging judge's sensitive son, banished to the family estate after a public rebuke, falls for a local girl whose family history entangles him with the very man his father once condemned. Stevenson's unfinished last novel.

books.title: Twilight Sleep
books.author: Edith Wharton
books.synopsis: A wealthy New York matriarch devotes herself to fads, causes, and painless-childbirth science to keep her family numb to any unpleasantness, while her son's marriage and her daughter's unhappiness quietly curdle beneath the anesthetized surface.

books.title: The Prime Minister
books.author: Anthony Trollope
books.synopsis: The scrupulous, thin-skinned Plantagenet Palliser becomes a reluctant coalition Prime Minister while his wife's political ambitions for him collide with his own doubts, entwined with the ruinous marriage of a young woman to a plausible foreign adventurer.

books.title: He Knew He Was Right
books.author: Anthony Trollope
books.synopsis: A young husband's baseless jealousy over his wife's friendship with her godfather curdles into an obsession that destroys his marriage, his reason, and finally himself, in Trollope's dark study of stubborn pride.

books.title: Ayala's Angel
books.author: Anthony Trollope
books.synopsis: Orphaned and shuttled between a rich aunt's household and a poor one, a romantic young woman refuses ordinary suitors while waiting for an imagined ideal 'angel of light,' until a real one finally proves worth having.

books.title: Three Men on the Bummel
books.author: Jerome K. Jerome
books.synopsis: The three friends from Three Men in a Boat, now married and middle-aged, escape their wives for a bicycling tour through the German countryside, bumbling through inns, bureaucracy, and each other's company.
